name: Dictation
description: Speak where the cursor is (a note, a terminal, the Ask box, a chat, any app's field with its keys): ⌘J starts and ⌘J again stops, or hold ⌘J while you speak. Words show dimmed as you say them and settle into the text, recognized by Soniox in the cloud with its key, else on this Mac: Apple's on-device recognizer, or Parakeet with Handy's or Hex's model. Fix a word right after saying it (here or in another app) and it's added to your dictionary (Dictionary.md), which every recognizer then expects. In a terminal the words go in as a paste and never press Enter. Move to another app or tab and it keeps listening, the words in a box under the menu bar: they land in the field in front when it stops, else where you began, else on the clipboard and in your inbox.

engine.label: Recognizer
engine.description: automatic: Soniox when its key is set (vau secret "Soniox API key" | vau dictation key), else Parakeet when its model is on this Mac and the language is English, else Apple's (macOS 26). Soniox streams to the cloud, any language; when it can't, this Mac's finishes. Parakeet is English only and uses the model Handy or Hex downloaded

language.label: Language
language.description: a language's code, like en or pt-BR, for Apple's recognizer; left out, the Mac's

languages.label: Languages you speak
languages.description: codes like en and pt: what Soniox listens for, switching between them on its own; left out, the language above and the Mac's

silence.label: Stop after silence
silence.description: seconds without speech before a tapped dictation stops on its own; 0 never: it listens until you stop it

fn.label: Dictate anywhere
fn.description: on a Mac, the dictation keys dictate in any app, as ⌘J does here (the companion has keys of its own)

keys.label: Dictation keys
keys.description: the keys that dictate: fn⌃ held together, or fn, a right modifier or Control alone; a tap starts and the next stops, hold while you speak, or double tap for hands-free. A key the companion talks with (its Talk keys) isn't one

microphone.label: Microphone
microphone.description: auto: the system's input, but with Bluetooth headphones out the built-in (or a wired) mic, so they keep their full sound (their own mic drops them to call quality); default: always the system's input; builtin: the Mac's own; or a device's name. A Bluetooth mic used anyway stays open until the companion's answer is said

keep_audio.label: Keep the last dictation's audio
keep_audio.description: what the microphone heard last, kept on this Mac (the app's logs folder, dictation-last.wav) to replay it when a recognizer gets words wrong; each dictation replaces it
